source.title: Redundant representations help generalization in wide neural networks ,
source.authors: Diego Doimo; Aldo Glielmo; Sebastian Goldt; A. Laio

record.file_problem: None; full paper text and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests test-error behavior across network widths and training time, and reports continuing improvement rather than the stated fall-rise-fall pattern. It also refines the account by identifying conditions for redundant representations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports width-sweep test accuracies, training-time test-error changes, and test errors for randomly selected neuron chunks. The chunk results use pruned subsets of a trained wide network, not independently trained networks of each chunk width. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper reports full-network width sweeps (Table 1) and training-time test-error curves for regularized CNNs and FC nets. These bear on whether a model-wise or epoch-wise peak appears. Every setting uses per-width tuned weight decay and label smoothing with clean labels. Double descent is not the paper's target; its aim is a mechanism for benign overfitting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors propose redundant last-layer 'clones' as a possible mechanism for error decreasing with width past interpolation (about W^-1/2). Clones appear only with weight decay and zero training error. They are absent when training stops early, when weight decay is omitted, or on non-interpolating ImageNet ResNet50s.
record.recipe_differences: Uses deep-network width sweeps, random neuron-chunk ablations, and representation reconstruction rather than an original double-descent protocol. The reported chunk-width measurements are from subsets of trained wide networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Redundancy depends on weight decay and reaching zero training error; the paper reports its absence without weight decay and on ImageNet models that do not interpolate. Results also vary by dataset and architecture, and the reported training-time changes depend on continuing training beyond the full network's interpolation point.

fits_no_version.finding: Random neuron chunks above a critical size (~ the interpolation width) act as redundant clones; chunk error decays as wc^-1/2 only with weight decay and interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued improvement past interpolation in regularized wide nets arises from redundant last-layer representations that act as an implicit ensemble.

fits_no_version.finding: With uniform regularization, variance peaks at W=32/64 (WR28, CIFAR10/100) and W=88 (DenseNet40), then decreases with width (Fig. S5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In regularized CNNs, variance peaks near the interpolation width and then declines.

record.problems: The tabulated width-sweep accuracies are averages over four runs, but row-specific uncertainty values are not stated in the text. Several test-error trajectories and chunk curves are presented qualitatively or in figures rather than as full numerical series. ImageNet models do not interpolate, limiting conclusions about that setting.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant reported width or training-time result was left out. Representation-reconstruction R2 and residual-correlation measurements were omitted because they do not measure the test-error behavior named in the claim.

untested.parts: Width sweeps without tuned regularization or with label noise; FC5 curve near interpolation (figure only).
Full numeric epoch trajectories; training with label noise or without weight decay.
All of it; sample size is not varied.
All of it; only neural networks are studied.
Label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, and a regularized vs unregularized full-network width sweep. No-weight-decay runs are reported only for chunks of one network.

missing.what: Test loss, bias² and variance vs width under a single fixed regularization (Fig. S5); the variance peak is stated, but whether test loss peaks is not stated in the text.
DenseNet40 training/test error dynamics on CIFAR10

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled the rows 'reversed' and the versions 'challenges'. But a monotone curve is an absent peak, and every sweep used regularization tuned per width with no label noise. Under those conditions the originals and V6 expect the peak to shrink or vanish, so limits_scope fits better than challenges. The ImageNet rows cannot speak to the interpolation peak because those models never interpolate.

versions.untested_parts: The width sweeps cover the stated datasets and architectures but do not test every network size or training protocol.
The text describes test-error changes during training for CIFAR10 and CIFAR100; it does not provide a numerical full-epoch trajectory for every architecture and dataset.
Training-set sample size is not varied.
The experiments concern neural networks and do not test the claim across non-neural model classes.
The paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and samples.

It compares regularized and unregularized training for representation redundancy, but does not test whether label noise drives a double-descent peak, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes such a peak.
The paper does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters to assess whether a second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

relation.reason: Full-network accuracy across widths and test error across training bear directly on V1 and V2, although explaining representation redundancy is the principal objective.

tranche.reason: The study investigates representation redundancy in regularized networks; its own width sweeps and training trajectories provide results on the claims in this setting.

source_check.notes: Monotonicity is established at sampled widths; the study does not establish that tuning causally removes a peak. CIFAR10 WR28-8 uses zero label smoothing, and the DenseNet40 sweep is on CIFAR10 only.

statements.correction: Figure 5: Wide-ResNet28-8, CIFAR10, weight decay 5×10^-4, label smoothing 0, cosine annealing; full-network training error reaches zero around epoch 160; both training phases reduce test error; improvement stops around epoch 180. The stated noise threshold belongs to another study.
statements.problem: The general absence-of-rise claim fits this study, but the named architectures and conditions omit its WR28-8 experiment; r26 does not substantiate VGG or ResNet18 controls.
